title: Client descriptor mapping and migration contract for model-alias deprecation
creator: Sofia Grant
description: This ticket defines the contract and operational plan to deprecate legacy model aliases (unversioned names used by older clients) and replace them with explicit model descriptors (model_id + version + descriptor metadata). The goal is to provide a deterministic, testable migration path for customers and SDKs, avoid silent behavior changes, and ensure we have telemetry gates and rollback conditions before hard-removal in runtime-1.21.
background: Over the last 18 months we have accumulated aliases like "gptx-legacy" and "embed-v0" that map to different model artifacts depending on internal routing policies. These aliases are causing regression risk during quantization rollouts and make kernel selection non-deterministic for Dedicated customers. Previous deprecation efforts focused on endpoint-level compatibility shims; this initiative takes a contract-first approach targeting the model identifier surface and client descriptors so clients can opt-in to explicit versioning.
scope_included: Contract definition for client descriptor payload (fields, allowed values, migration default semantics)
SDK changes: auto-mapping helper and opt-in strict_mode flag in JS/Python/Go
Server-side translation layer: read-only mapping table + telemetry hooks (no live rewrite)
Migration test harness: pytest and integration test templates for customers
Rollout plan with staggered telemetry gates and canary cohorts
scope_excluded: Removal of any models from model catalog (this ticket only changes aliasing semantics)
Billing model changes for embeddings or new token accounting
On-prem private control plane upgrade packaging (separate Private runtime upgrade ticket)
migration_contract: Clients will be required to send either a model_descriptor object or a legacy_alias string. When a model_descriptor is present, server will use it directly. When legacy_alias is present, server will consult the mapping table and emit a deprecation header and telemetry ping. A new HTTP response header X-Redwood-Model-Descriptor will include the resolved descriptor for observability. SDKs will expose a 'strict_descriptor' opt-in that rejects legacy aliases and fails fast with a clear error code 422 and migration_hint in the response body.
migration_steps: Publish descriptor schema v1 to docs and OpenAPI
Release SDK patch that adds auto-mapper and strict_descriptor flag (minor semver bump)
Deploy server-side mapping table in read-only mode and enable header emission for 10% of traffic
Run customer shadowing program for enterprise tenants (invite list) for 4 weeks
Increase header emission to 100% and start warning emails to customers using legacy aliases
Announce hard-rollback window and schedule removal date (>= 90 days after 100% warning)
acceptance_criteria: Schema published and referenced in SDK docs with examples for JavaScript/Python/Go
SDKs include an 'enable_descriptor_migration' flag and integration tests that validate header and 422 error behavior
Server emits X-Redwood-Model-Descriptor header consistently for 100% of test traffic in staging
Telemetry dashboard showing alias usage by client_id exists and is accessible to customer success

Two independent rollback criteria are defined and testable: (A) sustained error rate increase > 1.5x baseline for 24h in canary cohort, (B) model quality regressions where BLEU/ROUGE decline by >5% on pinned eval prompts
Legal and Security reviewed migration messaging and header exposure to ensure no PII leakage
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish PRD and open RFC with SDK and runtime teams
Week 2: SDK alpha release and internal dogfooding on non-prod accounts
Week 4: Mapping table deployed to staging; 10% header emission in preprod
Week 8: Enterprise shadow program (opt-in customers) begins; collect migration blockers
Week 12: Full production header emission; start customer warning campaign (email + console banners)
Week 24: Target hard-deprecation date (no legacy alias resolution in runtime; clients must send descriptor)
telemetry_gates: Gate A (adopt rate): continue only if at least 60% of active client keys have switched to descriptors within 30 days of full header emission
Gate B (error spike): abort and rollback if any canary cohort shows 1.5x error-rate increase sustained for 24h
Gate C (quality): abort if pinned eval suites show >5% drop in quality metrics after alias resolution change
Gate D (customer complaints): require manual review if 5 or more high-priority CS tickets are opened in 7 days referencing descriptor migration
rollback_criteria: Automated rollback initiated when Gate B or Gate C triggers
Manual rollback if legal/security discover header leakage or compliance violation
Rollback plan must include reverting mapping table to previous behavior and a fast-path toggle to re-enable alias passthrough for affected client_ids
